title: GPU unit tests fail to extract OpenVINO package - PowerShell execution policy disabled scripts on Windows runner
signature: cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: Extract OpenVINO packages step fails: PowerShell .ps1 script blocked by Windows execution policy

key_errors: . : File C:\actions-runner\_work\_temp\01e46bc1-589b-401c-a97e-b0622b633f59.ps1 cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system. For more information, see about_Execution_Policies at https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=135170.
root_cause: The 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step dot-sources a generated temporary PowerShell script (Expand-Archive invocation) via `. '<temp>.ps1'`. The GPU unit tests Windows self-hosted runner has its PowerShell execution policy set to Restricted (or similarly locked down), which blocks loading/dot-sourcing any .ps1 file regardless of its content, independent of the PR's actual changes. This is the 5th occurrence of the exact same signature on different runners/PRs in the last ~19 hours, confirming it is a runner/environment configuration issue rather than anything introduced by PR #39262 (an unrelated ARM/CPU softmax fix with no Windows/PowerShell/CI changes).
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires access to the specific Windows self-hosted GPU unit tests runner. Locally: run `Get-ExecutionPolicy -List` on the affected runner image; if `LocalMachine`/`Process` scope resolves to Restricted, any `powershell -command ". '<script>.ps1'"` invocation (as used by actions/download-artifact's Expand-Archive wrapper) will fail identically.
recommended_actions: Set the PowerShell execution policy to RemoteSigned (or Bypass for CI-only images) on the GPU unit tests Windows runner image/pool, e.g. `Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope LocalMachine -Force`, and bake it into the runner provisioning script/image so it survives re-imaging
Audit other Windows self-hosted runner pools for the same misconfiguration since this signature has now recurred 5 times across different workflows/PRs
As a workaround, have the workflow step invoke PowerShell with an explicit `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` flag instead of relying on dot-sourcing the default profile/policy
prevention_strategies: Add execution-policy verification to the Windows GPU runner image build/validation pipeline (fail image publishing if `Get-ExecutionPolicy` resolves to Restricted), and add a lightweight smoke-test workflow step that dot-sources a trivial .ps1 to catch this class of runner misconfiguration before it blocks merge-queue runs.
historical_context: Identical signature (PSSecurityException / 'scripts is disabled on this system') previously recorded 4 times in the last ~19 hours across runs 44059107723, 44054389090, 44051380184, and 43897852421, affecting PRs #39899, #39839, #39423, #39833 - none related to this PR's changes, confirming a persistent runner-level misconfiguration rather than a code regression.
